team_members.name: Connie Daya
team_members.bio:
Connie Daya is the Co-Founder and Chief Financial Officer of the Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF). With an MBA in Healthcare Fiscal Management and a strong background in financial accounting, she brings deep expertise in financial oversight and operational management.

Since co-founding WEF in 2009, Connie has led its financial and administrative functions, supporting the organization's growth and impact on thousands of children and youth globally. She is also actively engaged in community service and philanthropy, reflecting a strong commitment to giving back.

team_members.name: Kamal Daya
team_members.bio:
Kamal Daya is the CEO and Co-Founder of the Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF), which he established in 2009. With over four decades at New York Life Insurance Company—consistently ranking among the top advisors—he brings deep financial expertise alongside a strong commitment to philanthropy.

Under his leadership, WEF has expanded its impact to reach tens of thousands of children and youth across multiple countries, with a focus on education, skills development, and scholarships. Kamal is also actively engaged in global philanthropy initiatives and remains deeply committed to advancing equitable access to education.

team_members.name: Parvin Dhanji
team_members.bio: Parvin Dhanji is a business leader and strategic advisor with extensive experience in advertising, marketing, and corporate management. She has led multiple organizations, including serving as President and CFO of Imagineering, Inc., where she oversees strategy, finance, and operations. A Certified Mediator from DePaul University, she brings expertise in conflict resolution and governance, along with an academic background in English Literature and Advertising.

team_members.name: Shahin Paroo
team_members.bio: Born in Nairobi, Kenya, she moved to Toronto in 1974 and later to the United States in 1980. She attended the University of Texas, graduating in 1984 with a degree in Arts. She began her career at Citibank (1986-1989), working in sales focused on data capture solutions and credit card processing systems. In 1990, she transitioned into real estate, becoming a licensed agent and starting to invest in multifamily properties in Dallas, Texas. Today, she owns and manages a portfolio of approximately 500 units across five residential complexes in Dallas.

team_members.name: Ahmed Ghulamali
team_members.bio: Ahmed Gulamali is a retired management and project professional with extensive experience leading strategic initiatives across the fintech, telecom, and IT consulting sectors. He holds degrees in Computer Information Systems and an MBA. Alongside his professional career, he has dedicated over two decades to volunteer service in community institutions.

team_members.name: Karishma Ismail
team_members.role: Financial Literacy Advisor to women Entrepreneurs and Field officers of Bright: Beginnings ECLCs initiative
team_members.bio: Karishma Ismail is an executive coach, speaker, and leadership advisor with over 15 years of experience in leadership development and high-performance coaching. She works with founders, executives, and investors to help them scale with clarity, confidence, and alignment. She is also the founder of Live Your Legacy and Empowered Desi, focused on leadership growth, financial independence, and women’s empowerment.

team_members.name: Ishan Daya
team_members.bio: A tenured leader with over a decade of experience building organizations and leading high-performing teams of 200+ people toward a shared vision. He has led fundraising, strategic leadership, and operations managing budgets of over $70M, while recruiting top talent and driving organizational performance. His core focus is strengthening grassroots power and advancing the public good through community organizing and policy.

team_members.name: Alisha Daya
team_members.bio: Alisha Daya is a nursing leader and change agent focused on transforming nursing education and advancing professional practice excellence. She is a strategic leader and strong communicator with a proven ability to guide interprofessional teams through complex change. She has led large-scale programs, aligning education with organizational goals and evidence-based strategies to improve outcomes and impact.

team_members.name: Shairoz Mistry
team_members.bio:
Shairoz Mistry is an education and community impact leader with expertise in early childhood development, parent education, educator coaching, quality improvement systems, and culturally responsive programming. She currently serves as Senior Director of Community Impact at Children's Museum Houston, where she leads early childhood initiatives, community outreach, and evaluation efforts serving more approximately 1 million children and families annually.

Her career spans leadership roles in the United States and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), including Head of the Aga Khan Education Portfolio for the GCC, Curriculum Developer for the Aga Khan Education Portfolio (GCC), Manager of Mentors at Collaborative for Children, and National Project Manager for Pre-primary Teacher Mentoring and Coaching program at Ismaili Tariqa and Religious Education Board (ITREB) USA. At Collaborative for Children, she led a team of mentors supporting teaching and administrative quality improvement systems across 13 counties surrounding Greater Houston, primarily serving child care programs in low-income communities.

Shairoz is passionate about ensuring all children have access to high-quality early learning experiences and enter school ready to thrive, regardless of their socioeconomic, cultural, or linguistic background.

As a Worldwide Education Foundation Board Member, she is committed to advancing equitable educational opportunities and strengthening systems that support children, families, and educators worldwide.

team_members.name: Dr. Anita Hasni Mohammad
team_members.bio:
Dr. Anita Hasni Mohammad is a developmental psychologist, researcher, and international development consultant with deep expertise in early childhood development, child psychology, and education systems. She holds a PhD from Georgia State University, where her research examined the cognitive and social foundations of early childhood — including original work on Theory of Mind in preschoolers, investigating how young children develop social awareness and make sense of the world through visual and auditory experience. Her academic work spans developmental milestones, sensitive learning periods, and the ethical dimensions of research with children.

Bridging research and public policy, Dr. Mohammad worked as a Lead Research and Policy Analyst with the Georgia Department of Early Care and Learning (DECAL), where she led continuous quality improvement initiatives for state-level early education programs. She managed and evaluated Early Head Start–Child Care Partnerships, with a particular focus on sustaining high-quality services for vulnerable families during the disruptions of the COVID-19 pandemic.

In 2021, Dr. Mohammad founded Tesseract Global Consulting, a research and evaluation firm dedicated to translating complex data into accessible, actionable knowledge for practitioners, policymakers, and institutions. Through Tesseract Global, she has partnered with multiple United Nations evaluation offices — including contributing to system-wide gender integration evaluations and analyzing global progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 5: Gender Equality. She also serves on Georgia Tech's College of Sciences Advisory Board and on community advisory committees focused on maternal and infant health, reflecting her commitment to science in service of human potential and well-being.

Dr. Mohammad brings to the Herzing-Daya Research and Learning Hub a rare combination of rigorous scholarship, on-the-ground policy experience, and global development perspective. Her expertise in early childhood frameworks and systemic education evaluation makes her an invaluable guide as the Hub works to generate knowledge from the mountains — and translate it into impact for the world.

team_members.name: Samina Hussain
team_members.bio:
Samina Hussain, is the Executive Director overseeing Chitral Operations. Samina earned her BS in English Literature from Islamia College, Pakistan, and pursued her passion for cultural studies with an M.A in Muslim Cultures from the Institute for the Study of Muslim Civilizations, Aga Khan University International, UK.

Currently, Samina serves as a dedicated Executive Director at WEF/FES, where her responsibilities revolve around the seamless execution of Chitral Operations. Her adept project management skills, coupled with a deep understanding of diverse cultures, form the backbone of her impactful contributions.

team_members.name: Alamgir Khan
team_members.bio:
Alamgir Khan is the Operations Manager at WEF, leading operations across all programs. He focuses on translating organizational commitments into clear annual plans, milestones, and measurable targets.

With over three years of experience, he has managed large-scale program implementation and expansion, ensuring timely, compliant, and high-quality execution within approved plans and budgets. He has also overseen humanitarian interventions across Egypt, Jordan, and Turkey, supporting programs in education, healthcare, food security, and displacement response.

His role includes strengthening operational systems, SOPs, and controls, while leading budgeting, procurement, logistics, and audit readiness. He monitors performance through KPIs, reporting, and field oversight to drive continuous improvement, and coordinates closely with donors, partners, and senior leadership to ensure effective program delivery and sustainable impact.

team_members.name: Aftab Karim
team_members.bio:
Aftab Karim is the Project Coordinator for Bright Beginnings: Early Childhood Learning Centers and the In-School Language Labs Program in Upper Chitral. With over nine years of experience in the education sector, he brings a strong background in early childhood education, teacher development, and instructional leadership.

Aftab has worked extensively on curriculum development, language instruction, and teacher training, with a particular focus on Montessori methods, language acquisition, and inclusive classroom practices. He holds an MPhil in Education from the Aga Khan University – Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED), combining academic research with hands-on field experience in remote communities.

As a professional development trainer and curriculum mapping expert, Aftab has worked on designing impactful learning programs and assessment tools for both ECD and English language teachers. In his current role, he is committed to advancing holistic, sustainable, and community-driven education across Upper Chitral.

team_members.name: Sumbella Khan
team_members.bio:
Sumbal has worked in international education for over a decade. She obtained an MSc in Education at the University of Oxford, and studied Mandarin Chinese for her BA degree at SOAS, University of London.

She began her teaching career in 2007, when she qualified for her CELTA, and began to teach students English as a Second Language across China, England and the UAE. After gaining her formal qualifications and teaching experience, she worked in International Education across the the Middle East & North Africa region, with organisations like Cambridge University Press & Assessment, Oxford University Press, and GEMS Education.

One of her favourite quotes in relation to being a lifelong teacher and learner is:
'When one teaches, two learn'.

team_members.name: Asif Ullah Shakir
team_members.bio:
Asif Ullah Shakir is an accomplished graduate in English Linguistics and Literature from the National University of Modern Languages (NUML), Islamabad, bringing a unique blend of academic knowledge and hands-on experience. With four years of administrative experience in diverse multinational companies, he has developed strong organizational and communication skills that contribute to efficient operations and team collaboration.

Alongside his administrative background, Asif has experience in communication and digital marketing. Currently, he leads the communication efforts at the Worldwide Education Fund (WEF), where he is actively involved in content creation, fundraising campaigns, donor management, stakeholder engagement, and the operation of social media platforms and the organization's website.

His ability to craft compelling narratives, manage digital platforms, and build meaningful relationships enables him to strengthen WEF's visibility and impact.

team_members.name: Rashida Banu
team_members.bio:
Rashida Banu is a dedicated educator with over three years of experience in early childhood education. As the Early Childhood Coordinator at the Worldwide Education Fund (WEF), she plays a pivotal role in observing teachers and providing targeted training to enhance their teaching skills. Rashida holds a Master's degree in Education and a Montessori diploma with a focus on early childhood education.

Rashida holds a Bachelor's degree in Education from Jinnah University for Women, Karachi, and has completed a one-year Montessori diploma from the Pakistan Montessori Council. Her passion lies in fostering nurturing learning environments and supporting the professional growth of educators, ensuring that children receive a high-quality, enriching educational experience.

team_members.name: Mehwish
team_members.bio:
I am Mehwish, an Early Childhood Development Coordinator and advocate for the eradication of educational inequity. I believe that sustainable social transformation begins with strong, equitable foundations in early childhood education. With an academic background in Politics, Philosophy, and Economics and international study experience, I have developed a global outlook on education systems, policy, and leadership. This exposure has strengthened my understanding of how strategic vision, inclusive policies, and quality learning can transform societies.

I combine this global perspective with grassroots action: working directly with schools, educators, and underserved communities to improve educational quality and expand access to opportunity. My mission is to bridge the gap between marginalized and mainstream education systems and contribute to building a future where every child, regardless of background, has the foundation to thrive and lead.

team_members.name: Misbah Hussain Jan
team_members.bio:
Misbah Hussain is a dedicated development professional with a Bachelor's degree in Development Studies from the Institute of Management Sciences (IM Sciences), Peshawar. Misbah brings extensive experience in training, community engagement, and youth development. He has worked as a Trainer with UNICEF and the School of Leadership Foundation (SOLF) under the SHAMS project, delivering sessions on adolescent mental health, stigma reduction, and personal development. He has also contributed to community-based initiatives with the Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (AKRSP), supporting sustainable development efforts in underserved areas. Deeply passionate about the development of children through education, Misbah is committed to creating inclusive, empowering learning environments that enable young people to realize their full potential.

programs.name: Bright Beginnings: Early Childhood Learning Centers
programs.summary: Women-led social entrepreneurial model transforming dedicated spaces in private homes and schools into technology-driven Montessori-based learning environments for children ages 3–5.
programs.description:
Bright Beginnings: Early Childhood Learning Centers (ECLC) bring high-quality Early Childhood Development (ECD) opportunities to communities across Chitral, Pakistan, with a strong focus on remote and underserved areas. Each center follows a Montessori-inspired learning approach that nurtures curiosity, creativity, independence, and hands-on learning among children aged 3–5 years.

Montessori Learning for Young Minds

At Bright Beginnings, every classroom is thoughtfully designed to encourage exploration and discovery. Using Montessori learning materials, child-friendly furniture, and smart TVs for interactive learning, children develop foundational skills while exploring the world beyond their surroundings — from nature to different cultures.

Empowering Women Entrepreneurs

Each center is led by trained women entrepreneurs who receive professional training in Montessori pedagogy, early childhood care, and educational technology. These women are supported by assistant teachers, creating sustainable income opportunities and empowering local women to lead positive change in their own communities.

Integrating Technology in Learning

While preserving traditional Montessori principles, technology in our centers enhances creativity and engagement. Through guided visual content and interactive sessions, children explore global ideas while staying rooted in experiential learning.

Community-Driven Education

Parents and community members are vital to our success. Regular meetings and engagement sessions ensure that every BB ECLC remains a shared space for collaboration, belonging, and growth — where families and educators work hand in hand to support every child's journey.

Our Impact So Far

100+ centers launched across Chitral, serving 3,000 students, with 200 women educators trained and leading. Communities are actively involved in sustaining and expanding the initiative.

Our Vision for the Future

  • By 2030: 500 centers serving 15,000 children and 1000 women will be empowered
  • By 2035: 1,200 centers serving 36,000 children and 2,400 women will be empowered

WEF's investment over term of the project is projected to be 4 million Dollars / 120 crore Rupees.

Through Bright Beginnings, Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF) aims to transform early childhood education in Chitral, ensuring that every child has access to a stimulating learning environment, and every woman has the opportunity to lead change within her community.

programs.name: Government School Learning Centers
programs.summary: Integrating Early Childhood Development and Technology-Assisted English Language labs into primary schools across Upper Chitral for children ages 3–11.
programs.description:
This project is a collaborative initiative of Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF), USA, Foundation to Empower Students (FES) Pakistan, and the Elementary and Secondary Education Department, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The project brings Montessori-based Early Childhood Development (ECD) into government schools in Chitral for the first time, ensuring young children have access to structured, high-quality early learning during their most critical developmental years.

This initiative integrates two complementary components within government primary schools. In the morning, Learning Centers operate as Montessori-based ECD classrooms for children aged 3–5, providing structured, hands-on learning experiences that foster cognitive, social, emotional, language, and motor development. In the afternoon, the same spaces function as Technology-Enhanced English Language Labs, supporting primary school students in developing foundational English language and communication skills through interactive and technology-assisted learning.

Each Learning Center is equipped with Montessori learning materials, educational technology, and child-friendly furniture designed to create engaging and stimulating learning environments. Recognizing that quality education depends on well-prepared educators, the project also invests in teacher capacity building through teacher training enabling teachers and ECD educators to effectively implement Montessori principles and child-centered teaching practices.

By introducing Montessori-based ECD within government schools and strengthening English language learning, the project is helping to improve educational quality, enhance school readiness, and expand opportunities for children in underserved communities across Chitral.

Current Impact

  • Introduced Montessori-based Early Childhood Development education in government schools
  • Reached 2000 children through ECD and English language learning programs.
  • Trained 20 teachers and 10 ECD educators in Montessori and child-centered teaching methodologies.
  • Created inclusive and engaging learning environments that help bridge educational disparities between public and private schools.

Through this innovative model, this Project is laying a strong foundation for lifelong learning while advancing equitable access to quality education for children in remote and underserved communities.

programs.name: Government Model Schools
programs.summary: Transforming existing classrooms into modern learning spaces where our learning centers are established, serving children ages 6–11 with 25 dedicated teachers.
programs.description:
This project is one of the most impactful initiatives of Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF), USA, in Chitral Valley. It addresses a critical gap in early primary education within government schools by improving the learning environment beyond Early Childhood Development (ECD) classrooms.

For several years, WEF has strengthened early education through the establishment of Learning Centers, which integrate Montessori-based Early Childhood Development (ECD) classrooms for children aged 3–6 and Technology-Assisted English Language Labs for children aged 6–11 across 10 government schools. These centers have already reached more than 2,000 students and trained 20 teachers, creating engaging, child-centered, and technology-supported early learning environments.

However, a key challenge emerged: after experiencing vibrant ECD classrooms, children moved into Grade 1 classrooms that were under-resourced and not child-friendly. This sudden shift risked disrupting their motivation, confidence, and continuity of learning.

To address this gap, WEF launched the Model School Project, a focused initiative to transform the rest of the classrooms into welcoming, developmentally appropriate, and stimulating learning spaces. The aim is to ensure a smooth and positive transition from ECD to primary education, preserving children's curiosity and enthusiasm for learning.

With the support of dedicated Chitrali team and generous sponsors in the US, WEF has:

  • Renovated all the classrooms in 10 Government Primary Schools.
  • Created clean, bright, carpeted, and child-friendly learning environments
  • Introduced access to educational technology and interactive learning tools
  • Strengthened continuity between ECD and primary education

As a result, children entering Grade 1 now experience an environment that reflects the same warmth, structure, and encouragement they received in their early learning years—helping them build confidence and a sustained love for learning.

Growing Momentum through Partnership

This progress has been further strengthened through a formal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Foundation to Empower Students (FES), Pakistan and the Elementary and Secondary Education Department, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This partnership ensures long-term sustainability, institutional support, and the potential for scale.

WEF is envisioning setting up 600 more Model Schools by 2035 with projected investment of 2 million Dollars / 60 Crore Rupees.

programs.name: In-School Language Labs
programs.summary: Structured English language learning environment strengthening students' speaking and listening skills through facilitated technology-enabled instructions for ages 6–16.
programs.description:
In-School Language Labs represents a collaborative initiative between the Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF), USA, and its project delivery partner, Foundation to Empower Students (FES), operating in Pakistan. Functioning as tangible educational spaces, these Language Labs, established by WEF, aim to impart high-quality English language skills to students attending low-income private schools in Chitral Pakistan.

The chosen schools serve as dedicated hubs for the installation of English Language Labs and Career Counseling and Coaching Resource Centers. WEF/FES facilitates the provisioning of essential technology and internet-based content, obtained through licensed agreements with platforms such as Fluent U, Lingua Phone, and similar proprietary sources. Qualified English Language Facilitators, recruited and trained by FES, spearhead the delivery of English language instruction and career counseling resources within these labs. Importantly, these facilitators also play a pivotal role in training existing English language teachers at the schools, empowering them to assume leadership roles within the lab environment.

The primary focus of these language labs is to enhance the listening and speaking skills of students in primary and secondary schools. By fostering an environment that encourages the exchange of ideas and questions, the labs provide students with insights into the thoughts and actions of their peers in the broader world. Additionally, these labs serve as valuable resources for local teachers who may lack sufficient classroom time to address these aspects of language learning and face challenges in accessing relevant educational materials.

Current Impact

At present, there are 5 language labs operational at low-income schools in Chitral where we have around 1250 students enrolled who are being trained by 100 school teachers and 5 facilitators with the language skills needed to pursue higher education, vocational training, and improved career prospects.

programs.name: Teachers' Training Program
programs.summary: Building teachers' capacity to improve learning outcomes through in-person training at the University of Chitral and digital delivery for teachers in low/no internet settings.
programs.description:
English Language Skills Training for Teachers is an initiative of Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF), USA in partnership with Bridge Education Group. Bridge has offered and sponsored the three-month, self-paced, tutor guided, online Micro Credential TEFL certification to 08 teachers from the remote valley of Booni, Chitral in Northern Pakistan.

WEF provides the platform and necessary technology support to the teachers for taking the course which otherwise would not have been possible. To ensure active and effective engagement with the course, WEF organized weekly reflection sharing sessions. The teachers gather once in a week and share their understanding of the module and engage in discussion regarding the course. At the end of the course the teacher will do a practicum and submit a comprehensive assignment based on their understanding of the course. WEF will provide the practicum opportunities for the teachers at their In-School Language Labs to put theory into practice.

Current Impact

Under this program, 08 teachers received certificates in the first round of the training. We are currently impacting 13. So in total, we have trained 21 teachers to teach quality English Language skills and classroom management.

programs.name: Herzing-Daya Research & Learning Hub
programs.summary: Pakistan's first ECD research hub in a remote mountainous region, dedicated to producing locally grounded evidence on early childhood development and informing national policy.
programs.description:
The Herzing–Daya Research & Learning Hub is one of Pakistan's first Early Childhood Development (ECD) research hubs located in a remote mountain region. Hosted at the University of Chitral and led by the Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF), USA, the Hub is dedicated to producing locally grounded evidence that strengthens ECD practice, informs policy, and improves outcomes for young children in underserved communities.

Why Chitral?

  • Home to 52,000 children ages 3–5
  • More than 40,000 primary school students
  • Unique mountain communities often overlooked in education research

What We Do

  • Conduct research on early childhood development and school readiness
  • Strengthen ECD and primary education practices
  • Build research capacity through academic partnerships
  • Generate evidence to inform education policy and investment

Who Benefits?

  • Young children and families
  • ECD educators and primary school teachers
  • Researchers and university students
  • Policymakers and education stakeholders

Expected Impact

  • Stronger early childhood education systems
  • Smoother transition from ECD to primary school
  • Evidence-based, scalable rural ECD models
  • Research that informs policy and practice across Pakistan

programs.name: Secondary School Scholarships
programs.summary: Removing financial barriers for underserved students ages 14–16 in low-income private schools, supporting Grade 9 & 10 students across 5 schools with 115 scholarship recipients.
programs.description:
The Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF) USA, in collaboration with the Foundation to Empower Students (FES) Pakistan, is implementing the Secondary School Scholarship Program in Upper Chitral, Pakistan.

In this region, many students are unable to continue their education beyond Grade 8 because of financial hardship. Parents are committed to their children's future, often paying school fees even if it means cutting back on essential needs like healthcare. This scholarship program directly responds to that challenge. By covering tuition fees, WEF and FES reduce the pressure on families, allowing them to reallocate their limited resources toward other basic necessities while keeping their children in school.

WEF has a long track record of advancing education globally, while FES brings decades of grassroots experience in Chitral. Together, they form a strong partnership that ensures the program is both effective and deeply connected to local realities.

Current Impact

At present, the program supports 115 students enrolled in five private schools in Upper Chitral:

  • Oxford Public School
  • Orion School of Learning
  • Frontier Corps Public School
  • Alkhidmat Foundation School (Space Era Campus Booni)
  • Aga Khan High School Booni

For these students, the scholarships mean much more than just financial help. They represent encouragement, dignity, and hope. One student expressed it simply:

"Without this scholarship, I would have had to leave school to help my family."

Stories like these show the true impact of the program—restoring belief in education and building confidence for the future.

This initiative also reflects our wider vision: "We invest in the potential of children and youth across underserved communities in Central and South Asia. Through early childhood development programs, English language learning, and scholarships, we open doors to brighter futures—empowering young learners with the skills and confidence to transform their lives and uplift their communities."

Looking ahead, WEF and FES are preparing to expand the program to include students entering 1st Year and 2nd Year (Intermediate level). By 2026, our goal is to double the number of students supported, ensuring that bright learners continue seamlessly into higher secondary education without financial barriers.

The Secondary School Scholarship Program is more than an education initiative—it is an investment in a generation of leaders, thinkers, and change-makers who will shape the future of Chitral and beyond.

programs.name: AM Rising Stars Undergraduate Scholarship
programs.summary: Removing financial barriers to higher education by sponsoring selected students at the American University of Central Asia (AUCA) and UCA in Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan.
programs.description:
Launched in 2023, the AM Rising Stars Undergraduate Scholarship Program removes financial barriers that prevent talented young people from pursuing higher education and reaching their full potential.

Funded by Sadiq Ali & Family, administered by the Worldwide Education Foundation (WEF), the program provides deserving students from Tajikistan & Kyrgyzstan with access to world-class undergraduate education at leading regional universities.

Scholarship recipients are selected through a competitive process that identifies academically promising students with strong leadership potential and a commitment to contributing to their communities.

The program currently supports students enrolled at:

  • American University of Central Asia (AUCA), Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan
  • University of Central Asia (UCA), Khorog, Tajikistan

Beyond financial support, the scholarship program seeks to nurture a new generation of educated professionals, community leaders, and change makers who will contribute to social and economic development in Central Asia.

Impact

  • 52 scholarship recipients supported at AUCA.
  • 14 scholarship recipients supported at UCA.
  • 66 students provided access to quality undergraduate education.
  • Creating pathways to leadership, professional success, and community impact for talented youth from underserved backgrounds.

By investing in promising students today, the AM Rising Stars Undergraduate Scholarship Program is helping build a stronger, more educated, and more prosperous future for the region.

programs.name: Herzing Center for Skills, Innovation and Entrepreneurship
programs.summary: Integrated platform for professional development, teachers' training, vocational skills, degree and diploma programs including ECD, hospitality, travel, tourism, and technology pathways.
programs.description:
An Integrated Platform for Professional Development, Teacher Training, and Workforce Readiness.

Herzing Center for Skills, Innovation and Entrepreneurship is a comprehensive capacity-building initiative designed to strengthen human capital in Chitral and its surrounding regions. Hosted at the University of Chitral, the program seamlessly bridges the gap between education and employment by bringing academic learning, vocational training, and professional certification under one integrated platform.

Our Vision: To create a scalable, inclusive, and future-ready skills development ecosystem that equips youth, educators, and professionals with the precise competencies needed to thrive in evolving local and global labor markets.

Core Objectives

  • Forge Strategic Partnerships: Build and strengthen alliances with elite training institutions both within Pakistan and internationally.
  • Cultivate High-Demand Talent: Develop workforce-ready professionals tailored specifically for high-growth economic sectors.
  • Prioritize Practical Outcomes: Emphasize certification-based learning, hands-on training, and robust job placement support.
  • Launch Careers: Create highly structured, dependable pathways from initial training directly into employment and entrepreneurship.

Targeted Program Tracks

The Herzing Center for Skills, Innovation and Entrepreneurship delivers specialized diploma and certification pathways designed to meet urgent market demands:

  • Early Childhood Development (ECD): Transforming regional education by training the next generation of specialized foundational educators.
  • Hospitality, Travel, and Tourism: Equipping talent to lead and professionalize the region's rapidly growing tourism ecosystem.
  • Information Technology & Digital Skills: Building future-proof tech competencies, from basic digital literacy to advanced freelance capabilities.
  • Higher Education Progression: Creating seamless bridging pathways for students to transition into advanced degree and diploma programs.

Key Features & Ecosystem

  • Prestigious Institutional Anchor: Centered and hosted directly at the University of Chitral.
  • Unified Learning Platform: A singular, integrated ecosystem combining formal university degrees, professional diplomas, and rapid short courses.
  • Centralized Opportunity Hub: A single-window resource center tracking and distributing scholarships, job placements, and startup incubation support.
  • Applied Learning Focus: Heavy emphasis on industry-aligned skills and practical, real-world application over rote memorization.

Hybrid Delivery Model

To guarantee maximum reach and equity, the program is deployed through a highly resilient, blended delivery model:

  • In-Person: Herzing Center at the University of Chitral + 12 satellite hubs
  • Online: Zoom-based learning and offline-enabled digital platforms (Chip) for low-connectivity areas.

Who Benefits?

The program serves:

  • Youth & Job Seekers looking to break into the modern workforce.
  • Educators & Trainers seeking international-standard pedagogical skills.
  • Emerging Professionals looking to upskill and accelerate their career trajectories.

Funding & Support

The program is proudly launched and sustained through the visionary backing of the Herzing Family Grant. This foundational support enables the development of entirely accessible, high-quality training opportunities specifically designed to uplift and empower underserved communities.

Together, we can ensure that every child in Chitral has the opportunity to begin their educational journey with confidence, curiosity, and hope.
